title: #FactsFirstRedefined | Do all animals have Rabies?
explanation: Rabies is caused by a virus transmitted through infected mammals, usually through bites or saliva exposure. Not every animal carries rabies, but any risky exposure should be assessed promptly because the disease is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. Immediate wound washing and timely post-exposure vaccination are critical.
why: Dog bites remain common, and misinformation can either cause unnecessary panic or dangerous delay. Clear rabies education saves lives.

title: EXPLAINER | Medi‑sin of convenience: Over the counter, under the radar
explanation: Expanding access to medicines through small retailers can help remote communities, but it also raises questions about storage, dosage, counterfeit products, pharmacist oversight, and misuse. Convenience is beneficial only when safety standards remain strong. Certain medicines require professional guidance because symptoms can be misread or interactions overlooked.
why: Many communities are far from pharmacies and clinics. Policy must balance geographic access with safe dispensing and public education.

title: Cebu’s Warwick Barracks, Colonized Twice: First by US troops, now by private interests
explanation: Historic sites can be threatened not only by demolition but by privatization, redevelopment, neglect, or loss of public access. A former colonial military site carries physical evidence of a period that shaped Cebu and the Philippines. Heritage debates ask whether economic development can coexist with preservation and public memory.
why: Once historic spaces are erased, future generations cannot recover their physical context. Heritage protection is part of urban planning, not a luxury added after development.

title: What’s At Stake When We Call Disasters ‘Natural’?
explanation: Hazards such as earthquakes, typhoons, and eruptions may be natural, but disasters occur when people and systems are vulnerable. Unsafe housing, poverty, weak drainage, poor land-use planning, lack of warning, and inequality determine how much damage a hazard causes. Calling a disaster “natural” can unintentionally hide human decisions.
why: The country faces frequent hazards. Framing disasters correctly shifts attention from fatalism toward preventable risk and government responsibility.

title: EXPLAINER | Undoing the yes: A forensic reading of consent
explanation: Consent is voluntary, informed, specific, and reversible. A previous “yes” does not create permanent permission, and silence or inability to resist should not automatically be treated as agreement. Power imbalance, intoxication, coercion, age, and fear can affect whether consent is valid. Legal standards and social understanding continue to evolve.
why: Better consent education can improve sexual safety, relationships, reporting, and justice. It replaces victim-blaming with a clearer focus on mutual agreement and responsibility.

title: BAHA NA NAMAN: What makes flooding a political problem?
explanation: Flooding becomes political when budgets, zoning, drainage projects, waste enforcement, relocation, watershed protection, and urban development are shaped by government choices. Climate change can worsen rainfall, but repeated flooding in the same locations often exposes long-term planning failures. Political accountability should focus on systems, not only emergency response after streets are already underwater.
why: Flooding affects millions and consumes public funds repeatedly. Voters can demand measurable risk reduction rather than accepting annual disaster as normal.

title: EXPLAINER | Why going viral isn’t the same as getting justice
explanation: Viral attention can pressure authorities, mobilize donations, find witnesses, or preserve evidence, but social media is not a court. Online outrage may fade quickly, misidentify people, oversimplify facts, or reward the most emotionally compelling version of a story. Justice still requires investigation, due process, competent prosecution, and institutional follow-through.
why: Many cases gain attention only after trending. A healthy justice system should work even for people who cannot generate hashtags or media coverage.

title: The Devil Wears MAGA: Trump’s Nobel prize bid amid Israel-Iran conflict
explanation: Nobel Peace Prize nominations are often politically symbolic and do not themselves prove a candidate has advanced peace. Claims about Donald Trump’s role in Middle East diplomacy must be assessed against actual policy decisions, negotiations, military actions, and regional outcomes. Peace branding and peacebuilding are not the same.
why: U.S. foreign policy influences Philippine security, energy prices, migrant workers, and global markets. Filipinos benefit from evaluating international leaders beyond campaign messaging.

title: EXPLAINER | Why Cebu City Says No More ImPAWnding?
explanation: Traditional animal control often relies on impounding stray dogs and cats, but cities are increasingly considering sterilization, vaccination, registration, adoption, community feeding rules, and responsible pet ownership. Humane policy must also address rabies prevention, bites, waste, and population control.
why: Stray-animal management is both a welfare and public-health issue. Sustainable programs require local-government funding and responsible owners, not periodic removal alone.

title: HELL-TH CARE: Your body, their rules
explanation: Abortion debates combine medical ethics, law, religion, reproductive rights, maternal health, fetal life, and social inequality. In restrictive settings, women may still experience unintended pregnancy, miscarriage complications, or unsafe abortion, making access to emergency and post-abortion care essential regardless of political position. Policy discussion should separate medical facts from moral claims.
why: Reproductive-health rules affect maternal mortality, poverty, family planning, and access to care. The issue demands evidence, compassion, and legal clarity.

title: EXPLAINER | The proxy’s gambit
explanation: Iran and Israel have long competed through regional alliances, armed groups, intelligence operations, and indirect confrontation. Proxy conflict allows states to project power without always entering open war, but escalation can eventually produce direct attacks. The network includes complex local actors with their own agendas, not merely puppets controlled from abroad.
why: Middle East conflict can affect oil prices, shipping, OFWs, remittances, and evacuation needs. Distant wars can have immediate household consequences in the Philippines.

title: DEAD WATER: The hidden graveyard beneath Taal
explanation: The disappearance of people linked to cockfighting generated allegations, investigations, and public speculation about organized crime and possible disposal of bodies. Claims involving specific locations or methods require forensic evidence, credible witnesses, and official investigation rather than rumor. The broader issue is how gambling networks can intersect with violence and impunity.
why: Missing-person cases test police capacity, witness protection, and the rule of law. Families deserve answers based on evidence, not sensationalism.

title: EXPLAINER | Why divorce is a right, not a threat?
explanation: Divorce policy asks whether the state should provide a legal path to end marriages that are irretrievably broken. Supporters emphasize autonomy, protection from abuse, and practical relief; opponents raise religious, family, and social concerns. A serious policy design must address grounds, waiting periods, property, child custody, support, and protections against coercion.
why: The absence or design of divorce law directly affects families trapped in dysfunctional marriages and determines the cost and accessibility of legal separation.

title: EXPLAINER | Forging Maritime Security Ties with the PH-Japan RAA
explanation: A Reciprocal Access Agreement establishes legal arrangements for military personnel from two countries to train or operate in each other’s territory. For the Philippines and Japan, such cooperation is tied to regional security, disaster response, interoperability, and concerns over maritime coercion. It also raises questions about strategy, sovereignty, and escalation.
why: Security partnerships affect the country’s ability to protect maritime rights and respond to crises. Agreements should be understood beyond headlines about “allies.”

title: EXPLAINER | How the state failed the Filipino workforce
explanation: Worker vulnerability can persist even when employment figures improve. Underemployment, informal work, low wages, contractual arrangements, weak enforcement, unsafe conditions, and high living costs can make jobs insufficient for decent living. Labor policy should therefore look at job quality, not only job quantity.
why: Most households depend primarily on labor income. When work does not provide security, economic growth becomes disconnected from everyday life.

title: EXPLAINER | Reading between the man-ual’s lines
explanation: Men’s mental health is often shaped by social expectations to appear strong, self-reliant, financially capable, and emotionally controlled. These norms can discourage help-seeking and make distress appear as anger, withdrawal, substance use, or risky behavior. Supporting men does not require reinforcing traditional masculinity; it requires creating safer ways to express vulnerability.
why: Filipino men often carry provider expectations and stigma around emotional disclosure. Better mental-health literacy can strengthen families and reduce preventable crises.

title: EXPLAINER | Why the world has its eyes on Greta Thunberg’s Gaza voyage
explanation: High-profile activist participation in humanitarian missions can attract global attention to blockades, civilian suffering, aid access, and international law. Critics may view such actions as publicity, while supporters see them as a way to break media fatigue. The significance lies partly in how celebrity activism changes visibility, not only in the mission’s material impact.
why: Filipino activists, aid workers, seafarers, and migrants are part of global humanitarian networks. The story raises questions about the value and limits of symbolic action.

title: BINONDO: Where the past walks in changing present
explanation: Binondo is widely recognized as the world’s oldest Chinatown and reflects centuries of Chinese-Filipino trade, migration, religion, food, architecture, and entrepreneurship. Modern redevelopment creates tension between preservation and commercial growth. Heritage districts survive only when buildings, street life, businesses, and communities remain connected.
why: Binondo is evidence that Filipino identity has always been shaped by migration and exchange. Preserving it protects both history and living economic culture.

title: EXPLAINER | Changing the Guard in ‘Vote-Rich’ Cebu
explanation: Cebu’s large electorate gives the province significant influence in national campaigns. Political shifts there can reflect changing alliances, local dynasties, urban-rural differences, and candidate organization. Being “vote-rich” does not mean voters move as one bloc; local politics remain fragmented and competitive.
why: National candidates often design strategies around major provinces. Understanding Cebu politics helps explain coalition-building beyond Metro Manila.

title: HIV as an Archive Virus: reframing Its impact on the body and society
explanation: HIV attacks immune-system cells and, without treatment, can progress to AIDS. Modern antiretroviral therapy allows people with HIV to live long lives and can reduce viral load to undetectable levels, preventing sexual transmission when sustained. Social stigma, however, can remain even when medical science advances.
why: Rising HIV diagnoses among younger Filipinos make testing, treatment, sex education, and stigma reduction urgent. Fear can prevent people from seeking services early.

title: EXPLAINER | We’re not just a spectrum, we’re a constellation
explanation: Sexuality and gender are often described as spectrums, which is useful because identities are not always binary. The “constellation” metaphor goes further by recognizing multiple dimensions—identity, expression, attraction, community, and experience—that do not fit neatly on one line. No metaphor captures every person, but language can help people describe complexity.
why: More precise language can improve conversations about LGBTQ+ people without reducing them to stereotypes. Respect begins with allowing people to describe their own experience.

title: EXPLAINER | Political -isms: The propagandas you shouldn’t fall for
explanation: Political labels such as liberalism, socialism, fascism, communism, nationalism, and populism have specific histories but are often used online as insults rather than analytical terms. Propaganda works when a complex ideology is flattened into fear, identity, or a meme. Political literacy requires defining terms, examining policies, and distinguishing rhetoric from actual institutions.
why: Misused labels can polarize voters and shut down debate. Citizens make better decisions when they understand what political ideas actually propose.

title: EXPLAINER | Aid or agenda? The U.S.-backed Gaza humanitarian foundation under scrutiny
explanation: Humanitarian aid in war zones can become politically contested when delivery systems are linked to military strategy, donor governments, security screening, or displacement. Effective aid must be impartial, safe, accessible, and responsive to civilian need. When distribution mechanisms are distrusted, humanitarian assistance can itself become part of the conflict.
why: The Philippines frequently depends on and contributes to humanitarian systems during disasters. Understanding neutrality and aid governance is relevant far beyond Gaza.

title: EXPLAINER | Press Office Eviction: Today’s Carolinian Struggle for Press Freedom
explanation: Removing or restricting a student publication’s physical office can affect more than workspace. It can disrupt archives, meetings, equipment, production, source protection, and institutional independence. Administrative decisions should therefore be judged by process, necessity, and whether they indirectly burden critical journalism.
why: Press freedom can be weakened through logistics as well as direct censorship. Small institutional decisions can have large effects on a publication’s ability to function.

title: EXPLAINER | Meta: Fact-checking ends, crowd-sourced truth begins
explanation: Replacing professional third-party fact-checking with community-based notes shifts responsibility from vetted organizations toward users who add context to posts. Community systems can scale and incorporate diverse perspectives, but they may struggle with speed, coordination, partisan disagreement, and technical complexity. Platform design determines which corrections are visible and when.
why: Facebook remains highly influential in Philippine politics and news consumption. Changes to content moderation can directly affect the local information environment.
